sam: Heads-up, after rolling the new batching heuristics (0.9.3) yesterday we're seeing intermittent cudaMalloc spikes and increased tail latency on a subset of GPU workers. NSYS trace looks suspiciously aligned with kernel switches. Anyone free to eyeball? :thinking:
perf-bot: Trace uploaded: https://perf.example.internal/traces/1842507777.nsys :mag_right:
maya: Oof. Which params changed in the batcher? max_concurrent_batches / timeout?
sam: We increased max_concurrent_batches 8->16 and reduced batch_timeout_ms 12->6. Hypothesis: more small/short-lived batches causing allocator churn and pool fragmentation.
liam: Can you paste the NSYS kernel timeline snippet (the hot region) here?
sam: Sure, here's the clipped timeline around one spike:
```
[12:34:56.123] cudaMalloc 512 KiB (stream 2)
[12:34:56.125] attention_fwd_kernel<<<...>>>  (stream 1)
[12:34:56.130] kv_cache_load_kernel<<<...>>>  (stream 2)
[12:34:56.131] cudaMalloc 1.0 MiB (stream 3)
[12:34:56.135] memcpy H2D 1.5 MiB (stream 1)
[12:34:56.137] attention_fwd_kernel<<<...>>>  (stream 2)
// pattern: small cudaMallocs interleaved with kernels, correlates w/ tail latency
```
nora: Those interleaved host allocations right before memcpy look like pool fallback calls (pool couldn't satisfy the request). If the arena is fragmented you get cudaMalloc fallbacks which are expensive.
liam: Does the pool report any evictions or high fragmentation? Any logs from allocator with "pool.fallback=true"?
sam: I toggled debug on one instance and saw logs: `pool.alloc fallback to cudaMalloc at 0x7f8c... size=1048576` repeated rapidly during bursts. When I bumped pool_prealloc_bytes=256MB locally the spikes disappeared for that instance.
nate: I found a suspicious allocator change in commit ab12f3c — it altered the async fallback path and switched streams for cudaMallocAsync under some kernel selection cases. That could explain why kernel-switch boundaries now cause host allocations on different streams and break pooling heuristics.
maya: Nice catch. Can we revert that commit in staging to confirm?
deploy-bot: Rolling rollback of allocator change ab12f3c in staging at 1842510000.
perf-bot: NSYS + nvtx capture for reverted build available: https://perf.example.internal/traces/1842510200.nsys
liam: After the revert, do we still see the small allocation bursts?
sam: Not on the reverted staging runs. Tail latency drops back to baseline.
nora: Short-term mitigation: coalesce tiny batches in the batcher for 20ms when pool fragmentation is above threshold. Also add an allocator metric `cudaMalloc_fallbacks` to help detect this in Console.
nate: Long-term: adjust pool free-list compaction and avoid switching allocation streams during kernel selection. I'll open a follow-up PR to restore async fallback semantics and add unit test coverage for stream affinity.
maya: Action items: 1) Add `cudaMalloc_fallbacks` metric + dashboard 2) Revert allocator change in prod if staging looks good 3) Add batcher backoff to avoid flood of tiny batches 4) File perf regression ticket linking traces.
sam: I'll create the ticket and attach the NSYS + perfetto slices. Also will run a full fleet experiment with pool_prealloc_bytes=256MB as a canary.
perf-bot: Attached flamegraph + kernel timeline for the before/after: https://perf.example.internal/diffs/1842507777-vs-1842510200
deploy-bot: Staging rollback completed at 1842510450 :white_check_mark:
maya: Good detective work everyone. Keep the thread updated with the ticket number and any prod roll plan. :thumbsup:
sam: Will do — filing ticket now. Thanks! :eyes:
